title: Universal rank-one H0 gives a locally free first cokernel
statement: Let R be a commutative ring and P a cochain complex of R-modules. Suppose P^(-1)=0 and P^0 and P^1 are finitely generated projective R-modules. Suppose that for every commutative R-algebra B, the degree-zero homology of P tensor_R B is isomorphic to B as a B-module. Then for every prime ideal p of R, the localization at p of the R-module P^1 / im(d^0) is a free R_p-module.

source.place: Tags 00O0 and 00NX; rank-(n-1) unit-minor adaptation of 00O0, with the local-ring and residue-field H0 tests

proof.text: For every ring map R -> B, the scalar-extended degree-minus-one term is zero because extendScalars preserves zero objects. The short-complex homology projection is then an isomorphism. Compose its inverse and the explicit ModuleCat cycles/kernel isomorphism with the given H0 isomorphism. This gives ker(d tensor B) isomorphic to B. Lean helper h0_kernel_test proves this directly using Functor.map_isZero, moduleCatCyclesIso, asIsoHomologyπ and homologyMapIso. Test first with B equal to the residue field of A=R_p.

Apply new-residue-kernel-unit-minor to d^0 with the finite-projective hypotheses and the residue-field kernel test. It supplies a free A-module C, a map g:A->C, an equivalence ker(g) with ker(d tensor A), and an equivalence of the localized global quotient with C/range(g).

Apply the proved H0/kernel comparison with B=A. Compose with the kernel equivalence from the preceding step to obtain e:ker(g)~A. The inclusion composed with e inverse is an injective A-linear map k:A->A, so k(x)=x k(1). Its value c=k(1) belongs to ker(g). Therefore c*g(1)=0. In a basis of C every coordinate b of g(1) satisfies cb=0, hence k(b)=bc=0=k(0), and injectivity gives b=0. Thus g(1)=0 and A-linearity gives g=0. Lean helper kernel_equiv_ring_forces_zero proves this calculation.

Since g=0, range(g)=0 and the quotient C/range(g) is linearly equivalent to C by quotEquivOfEqBot. Transport Module.Free across this equivalence and then the quotient equivalence from the unit-minor step using Module.Free.of_equiv.
